newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan won't comment on report on higher UK output.
newsitem.headline: Nissan won't comment on report on higher UK output.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday it could not comment on a newspaper report that it had decided to start producing Pulsar passenger cars in Britain as early as 2000.

Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported in its Tuesday morning edition that Nissan planned to produce 100,000 Pulsars annually at its British subsidiary Nissan Motor Mfg (UK) Ltd in Sunderland, Northeast England.
A Nissan spokeswoman said: "What is said in the report has been rumoured in Europe for some time, but we cannot yet comment on our plans."
The Pulsar model, at present produced in Kyushu, southern Japan, is a subcompact with an engine size of 1400 to 2000 cc.

The paper said Nissan hoped to raise annual production at the British subsidiary to around 300,000 vehicles to maximise utilisation of capacity, making three models there instead of two at present. It made 229,000 vehicles there in 1996.
It said investment in the project was estimated at around 10 billion yen.
